newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Golds guide Australian stocks to firmer close.
newsitem.headline: Golds guide Australian stocks to firmer close.

text.p: SPI futures 2758 +16 US 30yr cl 6.40 -0.06
10yrbond futs 93.475 steady Gold NY 328.75 Lon fix 325.75
*Stocks close with moderate gains, early highs clipped by profit-takers, golds hold gains. Volume 328.95 million, A$748.78 value, 1,132 stocks traded, 306 steady, 488 up, 338 down.
A polished performance from the gold sector led the Australian share market to a stronger close on Tuesday despite seeing its gains trimmed in the afternoon.
The All Ordinaries index added 8.1 points to 2,731.9 after peaking in the first half hour of trade at 2,741.3.
September share price index futures contracts were 16 points higher at 2,758, a 26.1 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said business was at moderate levels with light gains in some of the leaders enough to overcome afternoon profit-taking in key miners, BHP and WMC.
BHP ended 11 cents lower at A$18.22 after peaking at A$18.54, while WMC ended steady at A$7.87 after hitting an intraday high of A$8.04.
"BHP and WMC got pegged back but the business was nothing exceptional," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.
Golds posted the biggest gains, the sector index holding near its highs for most of the day to add 2.6 percent, compared to a gain in the broader market of just 0.3 percent.
Normandy Mining, making up about 23 percent of the gold index, climbed 2.6 percent to A$1.59, while Acacia Resources jumped 2.8 percent to A$1.48.

Gutnick satellite Great Central Mining added 4.7 percent to A$2.65, while Newcrest Mining shone, climbing 5.7 percent to A$2.80, aided by forecasts of production at its Gosowong project and of a return to the black for its Telfer mine in Western Australia.
"Golds were the standout. The rest were neither here nor there," the dealer said.
Elsewhere, share registry services group Computershare climbed 20 cents to A$12.20 after announcing the purchase of two registry units from accounting giants, Ernst and Young and KPMG.
Australis Media added 2.5 cents to 21 cents after reinstatement to trading after news of its pay TV deal.

The deal would see rival operator Foxtel, owned by News Corp and government-owned telecommunications carrier, Telstra Corp, taking a controlling stake in Australis. The deal remains subject to due diligence and regulatory approvals.
News shares closed 10 cents higher at A$6.33, helped by a strong showing from its ADRs in New York trading.
Alan Jackon's Austrim Ltd jumped 42 cents to A$4.60 after Monday's sharp rise in annual profit to A$21.9 million and the setting of a 2-for-5 rights issue.
Looking ahead, traders said the market appeared well supported around current levels with hopes for an interest rate cut still uppermost in most investor's minds.
"That is certainly giving us a base but it is obviously a timing matter," the dealer said.
Wilson HTM's Scott Healey agreed, saying plenty of people appeared to be waiting for the Reserve Bank to act.
"A lot of people are just sitting on their hands until they see what the Reserve Bank is going to do with interest rates."
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about of seven to five, while about 27 perent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bonds yields tested higher during the afternoon session as the market showed some impatience waiting for next week's RBA board meeting and the expected cut in official rates. By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.54 percent, down from Monday's 6.55.

The Australian dollar showed scant sign of life after its offshore bounce with dealers reporting negligible interest from customers. By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the unit was idling at US$0.7367/72, having tread its recent well worn range, from US$0.7360/65 here late Monday.
